지문 설계: 근거 위치 — 앞: 화자의 말투(불평·농담) / 중간: 자기 정정·망설임 어구 / 뒤: 화자가 조용히 해 주는 행동 또는 피하는 화제. 직접 서술 금지 — 화자의 직접 평가어(admire, resent, grateful 등)와 '마음'을 말하는 문장 금지.

previous.passage: What is owed to a stranger met in a delay? I put the question to myself at the ferry terminal in Thessaloniki, where the steamer was held two days by weather, and where a gentleman named Emre occupied the bench beside mine and would not stop talking. He was travelling to a dying friend. He talked of whether to tell the man that his son had lost the family vineyard, and he talked of it badly, in circles, through too much tobacco. I found him tiresome, and I said so to the clerk, which was not unkind, exactly, only accurate. On the second evening I bought two coffees and set one by his elbow. When he began again about the vineyard, I did not turn the subject, and I asked what his friend had loved most about the vines.
previous.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Emre as conveyed in the text?
options: Growing sympathy for Emre despite a stated weariness with his talk.
Mild disdain for Emre despite a polite tolerance of his company.
Kindly interest in Emre despite wishing mainly to pass the delay.
Tired impatience with Emre despite finding him less tiresome later.
previous.explanation: 화자는 앞에서 Emre를 지루하다고 평가하고 직원에게까지 그렇게 말하지만, '불친절한 것은 아니고 정확할 뿐'이라는 자기 정정이 그 평가를 누그러뜨린다. 뒤에서는 커피를 사서 그의 팔꿈치 옆에 두고, 포도밭 이야기를 피하지 않은 채 친구가 무엇을 사랑했는지 묻는다. 이 행동은 말투 아래 공감이 자라고 있음을 보여 주므로 A가 정답이다. B는 말투만 읽었고, C는 관심의 이유를 지루함 달래기로 돌렸으며, D는 지문 어휘(tiresome)를 빌렸지만 행동 단서와 맞지 않는다.

previous.passage: Yona ran the crew that rewired the old apartment block in Lisbon, and on my first day he told me I held a screwdriver like a soup spoon. He said that sort of thing all spring. He timed my coffee breaks. He called me the intern in front of the tenants, though I was nothing of the kind. His plan was to finish the stairwell before the inspector came, working nights, and it worked: the inspector signed off on a Friday, and nobody on the crew so much as smiled. I told my sister he was impossible, which was not quite fair, I suspected even then. On the last night I stayed after the others, coiled the leftover cable the way he coiled it, elbow to thumb, left it on his toolbox with the ends taped, and went down the stairs without switching on the new lights.

Unspoken respect for Yona despite complaints about his harsh manner.
Dutiful gratitude to Yona despite doubts about her own skill at work.
Weary tolerance of Yona despite finding him impossible at times.
